extract:
Refused are a hardcore punk band from Umeå, a university town in northern Sweden that in the early 1990s became an unlikely global hub for vegan straight edge hardcore. Formed in 1991, the band emerged from the same tightly knit scene that produced acts like Abhinanda and Doughnuts. Fronted by vocalist Dennis Lyxzén alongside drummer David Sandström, Refused were active through 1998, reunited in 2012, and played what they announced as their final shows in 2025.

The group's early identity was shaped by American hardcore, particularly the straight edge and militant politics of the New York and Washington, D.C. scenes, filtered through Umeå's radical, animal-rights-oriented DIY culture. Their early material, later gathered on The Demo Compilation and The E.P Compilation (both 1997), along with the 1994 debut album This Just Might Be the Truth and the Everlasting EP, showed a fast, metallic, chant-heavy approach indebted to bands like Gorilla Biscuits and Earth Crisis. Lyxzén's lyrics were explicitly anti-capitalist and leftist from the start.

The band's sound expanded on Songs to Fan the Flames of Discontent (1996), released through Burning Heart Records, the Swedish label that became their long-term home. Guitarist Kristofer Steen and later Jon Brännström pushed the band toward heavier dynamics and more ambitious arrangements. That ambition peaked with The Shape of Punk to Come (1998), whose title nods to Ornette Coleman's The Shape of Jazz to Come. The album folded electronics, jazz passages, ambient interludes, spoken samples and dance rhythms into hardcore, anchored by the anthemic single "New Noise." The New Noise Theology EP followed the same year.

Refused collapsed almost immediately after the album's release. A troubled American tour ended with a basement show in Harrisonburg, Virginia that police shut down, and the band soon issued a manifesto-style statement titled "Refused Are Fucking Dead." That phrase also became the title of a 2006 documentary about their final period. Lyxzén went on to form The (International) Noise Conspiracy, while the other members pursued separate projects. In the band's absence, The Shape of Punk to Come grew from a modest seller into a canonical record. It was widely cited as a foundational influence on post-hardcore and metalcore bands of the 2000s, and "New Noise" became a fixture of film, television and video game soundtracks.

The band reunited in 2012 with a high-profile run of festival dates including Coachella, and their sold-out shows confirmed that their audience had grown in their absence. Freedom (2015), released on Epitaph, was their first album in seventeen years. It included the single "Elektra," co-produced by the pop producer Shellback, a pairing that drew both curiosity and criticism. War Music (2019) returned to a more direct, aggressive attack, with "Economy of Death" among its standout tracks. That same year the band was cast as the fictional group Samurai in the video game Cyberpunk 2077, recording songs such as "Blood Red" for it. This exposed Refused to a new generation well outside punk circles.

After decades of on-and-off activity, Refused staged a farewell tour that concluded in 2025. Their legacy rests chiefly on The Shape of Punk to Come, a record whose fusion of hardcore fury and experimental restlessness redefined what the genre could be. It remains a reference point for any discussion of Scandinavian punk's international impact.
title: Refused
